turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste either of our time. Who decided to put a zero in my son's gradebook before anyone picked up a phone and called me?
"Get this over with." That's how you're starting a meeting about a mark that could cost my son a scholarship? Answer me, Hale: was Owen heard before that zero went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My child never lies, and "everyone knows it" is not a document. Who is everyone, Hale, and who else have you been discussing my son with? I'm writing that down, and if that's all you have, I'm going to the principal's office when I leave this room.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
Is that why my son got a zero, because of what I do for a living? I'm writing that down too. Show me what you actually have on Owen's essay, or I'm going upstairs.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

I'm holding your school's own procedure, Hale: 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and 4.3 says software alone proves nothing. You broke the first one, and you haven't shown me anything for the second. Withdraw the zero today, or the principal hears about this before I'm back in my car.
